title: The Long Bridge
premise: In 1899, in a river city ruled by the victorious Republic's bureaucracy, apprentice clockmaker Casper Blackwood is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds hidden inside it a ledger proving the old monarchy's final night was not the treason the victors' historians recorded. When census taker Ilse Varga asks one question too many, Casper realizes his late master was the ledger's author—and that Ilse is hunting it for reasons of her own. Torn between loyalty to his dead master's memory, his found family of workshop misfits, and a growing love for the woman sent to erase him, Casper races to enter the truth into the official record before the century turns. He succeeds at terrible cost: the clock strikes midnight on New Year's Eve with the corrected account sealed in its case, Ilse chooses him over her commission, and the city begins—quietly—to remember.
about_author: August Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated private papers before turning to fiction. The Long Bridge draws on that experience with documents that outlive the regimes that tried to bury them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Casper Blackwood, POV. In his master's cramped workshop, Casper finishes a repair alone since Herr Aldous died, measuring his life in what can be carried. A summons arrives from the Royal Observatory—now the Republic's Bureau of Time. Emotional beat: grief disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Master Clock
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. At the observatory he climbs into the great clock's housing and finds a hidden compartment containing a coded ledger in Aldous's hand. He takes it without deciding to. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Census taker Ilse Varga visits the workshop with routine questions, then asks where Casper was on the night of the Abdication Fire—a date no census needs. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen.

chapters.title: The Found Family
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. The workshop's boarders—Marta the widow cook, young Tomas the runner, deaf engraver Piet—debate whether to trust the stranger watching their door. Marta resolves to protect Casper whether he asks or not. Emotional beat: fierce, unspoken belonging.

chapters.title: Reading the Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Deciphering Aldous's cipher over three nights, Casper learns the fire was set by Republican officers to destroy evidence the old king abdicated peacefully. Emotional beat: betrayal of everything he was taught to believe.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Dusk
chapters.summary: Casper and Ilse, alternating POV. They meet by accident on the Long Bridge; both lie about why they are there, and both know it. A wary, electric conversation about clocks and honesty. Emotional beat: attraction built on mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Bureau Wants
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Her superior, Director Kessel, reveals the census is a purge list and orders her to find 'the archivist's apprentice.' She realizes she has already met him. Emotional beat: duty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: Hiding in Plain Hours
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Casper hides the ledger inside a customer's broken carriage clock awaiting pickup, trusting the workshop's ordinary chaos as camouflage. Tomas nearly sells it. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Piet's Testimony
chapters.summary: Piet, POV. Through drawings and old letters, Piet reveals he witnessed the fire from the bridge and can identify an officer now serving on the Historical Commission. Emotional beat: the silenced finding his voice.

chapters.title: An Offer of Erasure
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Kessel summons Casper, offers him a comfortable post and amnesty if he surrenders 'his master's papers,' making clear refusal means the workshop burns. Emotional beat: terror wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: The Confession on the Stairs
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Ilse warns Casper obliquely during a scheduled follow-up visit, breaking protocol, and admits she took this job to find her father, purged in the same fire. Emotional beat: two loyalties colliding in one room.

chapters.title: Marta's Price
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta reveals she knew Aldous's secret all along and chose the family over the truth; now she tells Casper the family will stand with whatever he decides. Emotional beat: forgiveness freely given.

chapters.title: The Commission's Historian
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Casper approaches Dr. Ehrlund, the official historian, offering corroboration for the record. Ehrlund is sympathetic but powerless: the centenary volume goes to print December 31st, sealed by Kessel. Emotional beat: hope meeting institutional stone.

chapters.title: Tomas Follows the Runner
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Tomas tails a Bureau courier and discovers Kessel plans to raid the workshop on the 30th. He runs home through the snow, chased partway. Emotional beat: a child carrying an adult's weight.

chapters.title: The Raid That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Forewarned, the household stages the workshop's ordinariness while moving the ledger through the city sewers with Piet's help. Ilse covers their trail in the census rolls. Emotional beat: found family functioning as one mechanism.

chapters.title: Kessel's Trap
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Kessel confronts Ilse with proof of her interference and offers her father's file in exchange for Casper. She sees her father's fate was Kessel's own order. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Casper weighs fleeing across the bridge with the ledger versus staying to enter it into the record. He dismantles the master clock's strike train and rebuilds it to carry a second document: the truth, engraved in brass. Emotional beat: quiet, terrifying commitment.

chapters.title: The Night of the Thirtieth
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The raid comes; Marta is detained, Piet escapes with the cipher key, and Casper surrenders himself to buy time, telling Kessel the ledger is already beyond reach. Emotional beat: sacrifice without melodrama.

chapters.title: Midnight Mechanism
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Escorted to the observatory to 'verify' the clock for the centenary ceremony, Casper completes the brass insert under the guards' eyes—they cannot read a gear train. Ilse arrives with Ehrlund and the freed Marta. Emotional beat: coiled suspense.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. At midnight the master clock strikes twelve times, and each strike releases a printed page of the true account into the crowd below via the carillon's paper roll. Kessel moves to stop it; Ilse arrests him with her own commission's authority. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. In the aftermath, Ehrlund files the corrected history; Marta returns; Piet's testimony enters the archive under his own name. Casper and Ilse stand on the Long Bridge, choosing each other without paperwork. Emotional beat: earned tenderness.

chapters.title: The Clockmaker's Apprentice
chapters.summary: Casper, POV, years later. An apprentice asks Casper why the master clock carries an extra, silent gear. He answers: some things are built to be found later. Emotional beat: legacy, and peace.
